Dear Dr Meccam,
Re: Mr Jacob McCarthy, aged 82 years old

Mr McCarthy is being discharged today for your acute care after he underwent right below knee
amputation (BKA). He has recovered well.

Regarding his medical and social history, Mr McCarthy has been suffering from diabetes mellitus type 2,
hypertension, peripheral vascular disease, osteoarthritis, age – related dementia and benign prostatic
hyperplasia. Please note, his wife is the primary carer and he has a moderate cognitive impairment.

On 06 April 2018, Mr McCarthy was admitted with a complaint of two – weeks history of infected right             Commented [jc2]: a two-week/two weeks’
diabetic foot wound associated with a long history of non-compliance with diabetic medication. On
examination, His right foot was non-weight bearing and had pus, abscess and gangrene. Moreover, his              Commented [jc3]: h
blood cultures were positive for gram – positive cocci. Thus, he was given IV antibiotics.                       Commented [jc4]: he


Mr McCarthy will be discharged with the requirement of daily life activity assistance as well as continuity of
antibiotics and pain medication. It is worth noting that a follow up appointment has been made with a
vascular surgeon in two-weeks. In addition, his wife request for his home discharge was refused.                 Commented [jc5]: two weeks
